design-examination.name: Designs have a recorded evaluation scope

fields.title: Orbit R1 robotic vacuum
fields.statement: Fictional battery-powered floor-cleaning robot with suction, brush, navigation firmware and a companion app. Product targets, experiments and results are invented for engineering exploration.

fields.title: Pick up ordinary household debris
fields.statement: Clean the defined example hard-floor debris set with little intervention; learn which brush and suction combination is worth developing.

fields.title: Finish a useful cleaning session
fields.statement: Complete the intended cleaning task on one charge while maintaining predictable navigation and recovery.

fields.title: Fit into household routines
fields.statement: Allow understandable scheduling and quiet operation without making routine maintenance difficult.

fields.title: Draft debris pickup target
fields.statement: Collect at least 90% by mass of the fictional test debris set in the defined two-pass hard-floor task.
fields.acceptance: Invented design target; debris distribution, floor condition and procedure are controlled assumptions.

fields.title: Draft cleaning runtime target
fields.statement: Complete 60 minutes of the defined mixed navigation and cleaning profile on the selected battery configuration.
fields.acceptance: Invented duty profile; compare whole-product consumption and usable battery energy.

fields.title: Draft acoustic target
fields.statement: Remain within the fictional 65 dBA product target under the stated acoustic evaluation setup.
fields.acceptance: A draft target only; distance, room, operating mode and microphone setup must be recorded.

fields.title: Recover from obstacles
fields.statement: Detect the defined obstacles and recover without repeated user rescue during the example cleaning task.

fields.title: Simple schedule editing
fields.statement: A user can set a cleaning schedule and understand whether it has been delivered to the robot.

fields.title: Maintain the cleaning path
fields.statement: A user can remove collected debris and inspect the brush without specialist tools.

fields.title: Move air through the cleaning head
fields.statement: Provide the suction flow required by the selected brush and duct concept across the defined debris conditions.

fields.title: Agitate and collect debris
fields.statement: Use the brush and collection path to move the defined debris into the bin while avoiding the selected entanglement scenarios.

fields.title: Supply energy within the duty budget
fields.statement: Allocate usable battery energy among suction, traction, computation and reserve for the intended session.

fields.title: Limit heat during cleaning
fields.statement: Keep motor and driver conditions within their selected design limits throughout the duty profile.

fields.title: Follow and recover the route
fields.statement: Maintain pose and obstacle recovery while coordinating traction and cleaning actuators.

fields.title: Coordinate local and remote schedules
fields.statement: Store a usable local schedule and explain pending or confirmed remote schedule changes.

fields.title: Provide maintenance access
fields.statement: Provide accessible bin, brush and filter interfaces while retaining the air-path assembly.

fields.title: Control sound-producing operation
fields.statement: Coordinate blower selection, mounting and speed behavior with the selected acoustic target.

fields.title: Blower operating envelope
fields.statement: Operate the selected blower within the recorded duty envelope while providing the flow used by the example pickup profile.

fields.title: Brush and duct contribution
fields.statement: The brush geometry and duct path shall support the specified pickup task without assuming suction alone determines cleaning performance.

fields.title: Whole-product energy allocation
fields.statement: Allocate a draft average 60 W across the defined cleaning profile using the fictional 60 Wh usable-energy assumption; preserve reserve and profile assumptions.
fields.acceptance: Engineering allocation to investigate, not an engine-computed runtime guarantee.

fields.title: Driver thermal monitoring
fields.statement: Monitor the selected driver temperature indication and use an explicit derating behavior before the recorded component limit is reached.

fields.title: Actuator command timing
fields.statement: Deliver the recorded blower and traction commands without violating the navigation controller's allocated timing budget.

fields.title: Shared power-rail transient response
fields.statement: The shared rail shall retain the required controller supply during the defined blower-start and traction-transient scenarios.

fields.title: Obstacle recovery state
fields.statement: Record obstacle recovery and retry behavior so a failed route is distinguishable from completed cleaning.

fields.title: Persist schedule and delivery state
fields.statement: Persist schedule edits locally and distinguish a proposed app edit from the schedule acknowledged by the robot.

fields.title: Brush and bin access
fields.statement: Permit bin emptying and brush inspection while preserving the selected seals and duct alignment.

fields.title: Acoustic operating profile
fields.statement: Evaluate the selected blower, mounting and speed profile together against the acoustic target; no motor-only result represents the whole robot.

fields.title: Cleaning assembly
fields.statement: Physical assembly contains the selected blower, brush, duct and removable bin; its functions overlap with power, thermal and acoustic work.

fields.title: Baseline blower motor
fields.statement: Fictional blower option A used by the initial simulated build; retained as a distinct option from the higher-headroom concept.

fields.title: Brush and duct assembly
fields.statement: Fictional brush, air path and seals support pickup and maintenance access.

fields.title: Battery and power assembly
fields.statement: Fictional pack and shared supply electronics provide energy and handle actuator transients.

fields.title: Motor-driver board
fields.statement: Shared board provides blower actuation and monitoring, interacting with power supply and firmware timing.

fields.title: Navigation and control firmware
fields.statement: Native description of embedded pose, route, obstacle and actuator coordination; no source repository is connected.

fields.title: Companion application
fields.statement: Native description of scheduling, delivery-state feedback and maintenance guidance; no deployed app exists.

fields.title: Higher-headroom blower option
fields.statement: Alternative fictional motor option for a proposed build; changed load, mounting and acoustic behavior need evaluation.

fields.title: Actuator power interface
fields.statement: Record supply limits, expected transients and controller supply needs between battery/power and motor-driver work.

fields.title: Blower command and monitoring interface
fields.statement: Record command timing, duty representation and temperature feedback between firmware and driver work.

fields.title: Schedule delivery contract
fields.statement: Record schedule version and acknowledgment behavior between the app and the robot's persistent schedule service.

fields.title: Blower-control firmware design
fields.statement: Example blower-control design increases the proposed maximum duty from its baseline profile to improve pickup. Review energy, thermal, acoustic and command-timing effects before adoption; earlier baseline results remain captured against v1.

fields.title: Baseline blower installation drawing
fields.statement: Example drawing specifies motor option A, mounting and the selected duct interface.

fields.title: Brush duct and service-access drawing
fields.statement: Example assembly drawing defines brush geometry, bin release, filter access and seal location.

fields.title: Battery and power schematic
fields.statement: Example schematic and energy allocation describe pack use, shared rail and transient supply needs.

fields.title: Driver board and thermal design
fields.statement: Example board design covers blower switching, monitoring and thermal path; limits remain selected assumptions.

fields.title: Navigation scheduling design
fields.statement: Example firmware design coordinates route recovery with control-task timing and reports incomplete cleaning.

fields.title: Schedule persistence and app feedback
fields.statement: Example client/robot design captures schedule revisions and acknowledgment, retaining proposed changes during offline periods.

fields.title: Acoustic mounting and speed-profile plan
fields.statement: Example mounting and operating profile define the configuration to be evaluated; no acoustic result exists.

fields.title: Alternative blower installation proposal
fields.statement: Proposed option-B installation differs in mounting and electrical loading; it has not been incorporated into an evaluated build.

fields.title: Baseline blower and existing duct
fields.statement: Keep the initial integrated concept and investigate the pickup shortfall through brush and duct changes.

fields.title: Higher-headroom blower
fields.statement: Increase available suction by changing motor selection, accepting potential energy, thermal, acoustic and mounting consequences.

fields.title: Variable suction by cleaning condition
fields.statement: Investigate adaptive speed behavior to preserve runtime; this adds sensing, control and evaluation work before any benefit is established.

fields.title: Compare pickup concepts
fields.statement: Plan controlled comparisons of brush/duct refinement and higher suction using the same defined debris and floor conditions.

fields.title: Characterize combined power and heat
fields.statement: Plan simultaneous logging of supply, driver temperature and commanded duty for the proposed blower concept.

fields.title: Evaluate schedule feedback comprehension
fields.statement: Plan user tasks comparing pending/confirmed schedule feedback; no representative users have been observed.
fields.purpose: Investigate whether the proposed interaction is understandable.

fields.title: Hold blower selection pending combined evidence
fields.statement: Keep baseline option A as the recorded starting design and compare alternatives before selecting option B.
fields.alternatives: Brush/duct refinement; higher-headroom motor; adaptive suction.
fields.consequences: Motor-only pickup evidence will not resolve runtime, thermal or acoustic tradeoffs.

fields.title: Keep schedules locally usable
fields.statement: Use local schedule persistence with visible remote acknowledgment state in the fictional product design.
fields.alternatives: Require a live connection for every edit; silently treat app edits as confirmed.
fields.consequences: Needs version conflict and delivery-state evaluation.

fields.title: Prototype A — recorded configuration
fields.statement: Selected baseline design and criterion records for simulated evaluations. Exact native revisions are stored in the immutable capture; this record does not establish an assembled prototype or physical build.
fields.scope: Selected native revisions for fictional baseline prototype; an immutable native input set is captured separately; no physical build exists.

fields.title: Prototype B — proposed configuration
fields.statement: Proposed input selection substitutes the option-B installation design. It differs from the baseline selection but has no assembled prototype, executed evaluation or acceptance.
fields.scope: Proposed option-B configuration; no executed evidence.

fields.title: Baseline pickup evaluation
fields.statement: Evaluate the selected blower, brush and duct configuration against the defined hard-floor debris task.
fields.method: Defined two-pass task and debris-mass weighing; conditions and configuration must be identified.
fields.purpose: Assess integrated pickup performance; a single component result does not establish it.

fields.title: Whole-product energy evaluation
fields.statement: Assess whole-product power over the declared cleaning duty profile against its energy-allocation assumptions.
fields.method: Whole-product power trace under the selected profile and usable-energy assumptions.
fields.purpose: Evaluate the energy allocation; separate old captured inputs from the current proposed control profile.

fields.title: Driver thermal evaluation
fields.statement: Investigate driver temperature and derating under the selected sustained-load condition.
fields.method: Selected load/temperature record; combined high-suction conditions need separate coverage.
fields.purpose: Assess the selected thermal/derating scenario, not every operating combination.

fields.title: Shared power-interface evaluation
fields.statement: Evaluate shared-rail behavior during the declared combined blower-start and traction transient.
fields.method: Combined-load transient record at the selected power interface and configuration.
fields.purpose: Assess controller-supply retention in the declared scenario.

fields.title: Whole-robot acoustic evaluation
fields.statement: Define the whole-robot acoustic setup and selected blower/mounting/speed profile; no run is recorded.
fields.purpose: Evaluate the acoustic target using the whole robot; no motor-only proxy.
fields.method: Draft setup requires operating mode, distance, room and microphone conditions before execution.

fields.title: Schedule delivery evaluation
fields.statement: Define interrupted-delivery, restart and revision-conflict checks for local/remote schedule behavior; no execution is recorded.
fields.purpose: Assess engineering delivery behavior; representative-user comprehension remains EXP-R03 work.
fields.method: Draft delivery-interruption, restart and revision-conflict scenarios.

fields.title: Baseline pickup below the draft target
fields.statement: The simulated pickup finding motivates comparing concepts; it does not establish which motor or air-path change is best.

fields.title: Energy evidence predates profile change
fields.statement: The stored energy receipt captures the baseline firmware design. The edited duty profile creates a reason to review that evidence.

fields.title: Shared-rail reset remains open
fields.statement: The simulated transient failure connects motor loading to controller behavior and navigation recovery.

fields.title: Acoustic evidence is absent
fields.statement: A defined acoustic evaluation has no result. Increasing suction leaves an unresolved quiet-operation question.

fields.title: Blower-profile change assessment
fields.statement: Review recorded connections from the blower-control edit to pickup, runtime, heat, sound, command timing and prior evidence. These are explicit assessment subjects, not inferred technical consequences.
fields.scope: Selected connected functions, interfaces, design and evidence.

fields.title: Option-B motor substitution assessment
fields.statement: Assess mounting, driver loading, supply transients, control envelope and production setup before adopting the proposed motor configuration.
fields.scope: No release or manufacturing qualification recorded.

fields.title: Orbit R1 engineering release candidate
fields.statement: Fictional candidate remains open because pickup, shared-rail behavior, updated energy evidence, acoustics and user interaction have unresolved work.
fields.disposition: A human review is required; no automatic readiness score exists.
